claims.text: The local catalog models Pokemon Card Fan Club July 1999 as a one-row unnumbered promotional source group containing Tropical Present at source index 117.
Bulbapedia's unnumbered promotional list identifies source row 117 as Tropical Present [Postcard], Special Card, distributed through Pokemon Card Fan Club in July 1999.
Bulbapedia describes Tropical Present as a Fan Club object connected to GET Points, with copies sent to members and additional points awarded back to the account.
Bulbapedia identifies the Summer 1999 Tropical Present print as illustrated by Naoyo Kimura.

Bulbapedia says the July 1999 Tropical Present reprint used artwork from the Southern Islands Sea scene, while the earlier 1999 print was illustrated by Atsuko Nishida and the Summer 2001 e-card print used new artwork by Hiromi Ito.

The July 1999 Tropical Present matters because it shows Pokemon's early card culture remixing its own scenes: a Southern Islands image becomes Fan Club mail, and a gift-card mechanic remains tied to the membership account.

Agents should preserve Fan Club July 1999 route, Tropical Present name, postcard / Special Card / jumbo format, Southern Islands Sea-scene artwork, Naoyo Kimura credit, and non-equivalence with January 1999 and Summer 2001 Tropical Present prints before accepting a match.

steps: Confirm the route is Pokemon Card Fan Club July 1999 / Summer 1999, not January 1999 or Summer 2001.
Confirm the object is Tropical Present [Postcard], Special Card, and jumbo-format rather than a standard-size set card.
Check for Southern Islands Sea-scene artwork and Naoyo Kimura credit when matching this July print.
Separate the January 1999 Atsuko Nishida Tropical Present and the Summer 2001 Hiromi Ito e-card-stock Tropical Present.

Separate Tropical Mega Battle / Tropical Wind / tropical-themed promos unless source evidence proves this exact Fan Club row.
Request seller front/back photos and size/context evidence separately from catalog identity.

narrative.human_title: Tropical Present, July 1999: the island scene becomes Fan Club mail
narrative.why_it_matters: This print is where the catalog has to care about assembly rather than just name. Tropical Present is still a postcard-like Special Card, still part of the Fan Club point loop, but the July version changes the visual memory by borrowing the Southern Islands Sea scene. That makes it a little archive of Pokemon's summer machinery: membership, points, jumbo mail, art reuse, and a tropical image traveling from one product grammar into another.

narrative.human_title: Tropical Present 117: same name, new summer skin
narrative.why_it_matters: This is the collector trap and the charm in one object. The name says Tropical Present again, but the July 1999 card carries a different memory: Southern Islands art, Kimura's scene language, and Fan Club points moving through a postcard-sized object. It is not enough for an agent to know the title. It has to know which summer the title belongs to.
